name: SEQUENTIAL_RESEED
decides: Tells the caller that a pattern's warm start was rejected and the pattern was refitted cold from the initial models, quoting the warm rung's Rwp (or what it raised) against the cold one.
without: The caller would see only SeriesEntry.reseeded and rwp_warm, with nothing in the diagnostics saying the chain was broken at that pattern.
provenance: WP-0505 (src/rietx/sequential.py:22-26); WP-1051 the ladder; WP-1333 the raised-rung text (src/rietx/sequential.py:2017-2020); WP-1469 the diverged/above-fence variants (src/rietx/sequential.py:2021-2033)
families: synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp (tests/test_sequential.py:795, reseed_factor=1.0 forced)
synthetic LaB6 with an injected raise (tests/test_series_error_policy.py:302)
note: Fires only when the kept rung is cold; a warm_staged rescue sets rwp_warm and rungs_tried but no code. Its trigger is _reseed_needed (RESEED_FACTOR's fence or divergence), so its tier follows those rows. One literal level (warning).

name: SEQUENTIAL_RESEED.suggestion
decides: Points the reader at SEQUENTIAL_UNRECOVERED or SEQUENTIAL_RWP_OUTLIER when the cold rung diverged or is still above the fence, else at a specimen or model change at that point.
without: A reseeded pattern would carry no next step, and a reseed beside an outlier would read as a good fit (the contradiction WP-1469 removed).
note: One site, three texts; the walk counts the site, not the branches.

name: SEQUENTIAL_RWP_OUTLIER
decides: Names a pattern whose best rung is still above its rwp_fence, quoting GoF and Rexp against the last pattern inside the fence, and says its steps are left out of the discontinuity scan.
without: A blank or bad frame's kept fit would read as an ordinary trajectory point (issue #481), visible only by comparing each entry's Rwp with its rwp_fence.
record: SeriesEntry.rwp_fence; SeriesEntry.above_fence (a property, not a stored field); SeriesEntry.rungs_tried
provenance: WP-1469, issue #481; three measured causes in the docstring (src/rietx/sequential.py:2076-2085): blank frame GoF 1.00 vs 1.06 and Rexp 0.159 vs 0.040, counts fallen 4x GoF 1.08 vs 1.04, unmodelled phase GoF 16.7
families: synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp with a blank frame (tests/test_sequential.py:1247)
planted perovskite cooling ramp, synthetic, second phase and transition (tests/test_planted_series.py:130, tests/test_planted_series.py:146)
IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real, never fires (tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:286-289)
note: Reports and does not judge (docstring). Its threshold is the RESEED_FACTOR fence; the same verdict gates the WP-1469 carve-out and the discontinuity scan's rejected set (src/rietx/sequential.py:2389-2390).

name: SEQUENTIAL_RWP_OUTLIER.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to open the pattern's own fit before reading its values, and to refit with reseed on first when the ladder stopped short of its cold rung.
without: The reader would not know whether a cold start was ever tried on the outlier.
note: Two texts at one site, keyed on whether 'cold' is in rungs_tried.

name: SEQUENTIAL_UNRECOVERED
decides: Names a pattern whose kept attempt is still diverged after every rung the chain tried, and states that it seeded no successor and was left out of the series median.
without: The caller would have SeriesEntry.status == 'diverged' but no statement that the chain stepped over the pattern.
families: synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp, dictated divergence (tests/test_sequential.py:1158)
synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp, a quarantined pattern's variable (tests/test_sequential.py:637)
IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real, never fires (tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:284-285)
note: The report of quarantine, one of Rule 1's protections. It names neither the successor that warm-started from the last accepted pattern instead nor that pattern (README § Quarantine's record).

name: SEQUENTIAL_UNRECOVERED.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to fit the diverged pattern on its own to find out why.
without: A quarantined pattern would carry no next step.

name: SEQUENTIAL_CANCELLED
decides: Says how many of how many patterns the chain reached before a cancel, the pattern in flight abandoned and the rest never started.
without: A cancelled series' short entries list would read as a shorter series that ran to completion.
opt_in: cancel=None (default); fires only on the caller's own token or a stop written by rietx watch (runs.CANCEL_FILE)
provenance: WP-1016 (src/rietx/sequential.py:2151-2157); WP-1006's rule one rank up (src/rietx/sequential.py:112-118)
note: Reports the requested act and moves nothing. No field holds the series length, so the n of N lives only in the message. A recorded fit always carries a token (runs.attach_cancel, src/rietx/sequential.py:1273), but only a person or the caller sets it.

name: SEQUENTIAL_CANCELLED.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to re-run the series to extend the trajectory.
without: A cancelled series would carry no next step.
opt_in: cancel=None (default)

name: SEQUENTIAL_PATH_CHECK_INCOMPLETE
where: src/rietx/sequential.py:2168-2189 (warning, raise 2182); src/rietx/sequential.py:2191-2240 (info, raises 2218, 2227); called src/rietx/sequential.py:1369-1372, 1395-1396, 1418-1423, 3057
decides: Says the forward/backward comparison did not run (warning: a chain cancelled, or the backward chain raised) or ran on less than the series (info: patterns one chain has no entry for, paths no pattern could judge in both chains).
without: Zero SEQUENTIAL_PATH_DEPENDENT findings would read the same whether the comparison ran clean or never ran (issue #224's series C).
opt_in: direction='forward' (default); fires only under direction='both'
families: synthetic LaB6 with an injected raise (tests/test_series_error_policy.py:375, tests/test_series_error_policy.py:402, tests/test_series_error_policy.py:427, tests/test_series_error_policy.py:453)
note: Two literal levels at its raise sites (warning 2182; info 2218, 2227): two consequences in one code, which the record's 'two codes, never a threshold between levels' clause reaches. The info half names only paths some chain measured (a package choice that moves no value). The warning half's record is the diagnostic alone.

name: SEQUENTIAL_PATH_CHECK_INCOMPLETE.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to re-run direction='both' to completion, to treat named patterns as unchecked, or to read both trajectories of an unjudged path before quoting it.
without: A partial comparison would carry no next step.
opt_in: direction='forward' (default)
families: synthetic LaB6 with an injected raise (tests/test_series_error_policy.py:402)

name: SERIES_PATTERN_FAILED
decides: Names a pattern on which every rung raised, so it has no entry, and on the backward pass that the path-dependence comparison cannot judge it.
without: A gap left by on_error='carry' or 'skip' would read as a pattern nobody asked to fit, held only in SeriesResult.failures.
families: synthetic LaB6 with an injected LinAlgError (tests/test_series_error_policy.py:188, tests/test_series_error_policy.py:329, tests/test_series_error_policy.py:402)
note: Not in the brief's list; raised only in sequential.py, so 2003 owns it. Its injected error copies the private trigger series' LinAlgError, nothing else of it (tests/test_series_error_policy.py:1-22).

name: SERIES_PATTERN_FAILED.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to fit the failed pattern on its own and read the exception.
without: A failed pattern would carry no next step.
families: synthetic LaB6 with an injected raise (tests/test_series_error_policy.py:188)

name: SEQUENTIAL_DISCONTINUITY
decides: Flags, per path, the single largest step that exceeds DISCONTINUITY_FACTOR x the median absolute step and DISCONTINUITY_SIGMA combined esds, skipping relative paths and steps into or out of rejected patterns.
without: The trajectory would carry no named jump; a step would be found only by differencing trajectory(path) by hand.
record: SeriesResult.discontinuities (SeriesStep: path, labels, indices, signed step)
provenance: WP-0505 thresholds, rationale only (src/rietx/sequential.py:219-225); WP-1469 the rejected-step drop (src/rietx/sequential.py:2375-2386, issue #481); WP-1305 verification; WP-1333 relative paths; #604 angles modulo a turn
families: synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp, silent on a uniform ramp (tests/test_sequential.py:2015)
planted perovskite cooling ramp, synthetic and its null (tests/test_planted_series.py:112, tests/test_planted_series.py:208)
note: The maintainer's example (WP Context): to become SeriesResult.steps with no threshold and no diagnostic. Readers of the flagged pairs today: SeriesResult.discontinuities, the trajectory plot's shading (tests/test_sequential.py:1739), _verify_discontinuities (src/rietx/sequential.py:1350), the series deliverable (tests/test_termination_view.py:439). Level info. The verification pass appends to its message and suggestion with += (src/rietx/sequential.py:1880-1900), which the suggestion walk does not count.

name: SEQUENTIAL_DISCONTINUITY.suggestion
where: src/rietx/sequential.py:2437-2438; appended at src/rietx/sequential.py:1896-1900 by the verification pass
decides: Tells the reader to check the pattern's own fit before reading the jump as physics; after verification it adds how to read the cold/chain ratio.
without: A flagged jump would carry no next step.
note: The appended reading is outside the walk's count (an AugAssign, not a suggestion= keyword). The skill's references/series.md carried the symmetry-mode reading (WP Context).

name: SEQUENTIAL_PATH_DEPENDENT
decides: Under direction='both', names a path whose forward and backward values at the same pattern differ by more than PATH_DEPENDENCE_SIGMA combined esds and above the noise floor, judged only where both chains measured an esd.
without: The caller would hold SeriesResult.backward and both trajectories with no statement of where they disagree.
opt_in: direction='forward' (default); the GUI series panel defaults to 'forward' too (src/rietx/gui/series.py:80)
provenance: WP-0505; WP-1076 SeriesResult.backward; WP-1333 relative paths and label pairing (src/rietx/sequential.py:2988-2999); #604 angles
families: synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp, silent on a clean series (tests/test_sequential.py:2026)
note: The switch is opt-in but PATH_DEPENDENCE_SIGMA (3.0) and NOISE_FLOOR_REL are package numbers used once it is on, and they decide whether the verdict exists, so caller condition 2 fails for this code. Root CLAUDE.md calls it the only check separating a measured trajectory from an ordering artefact; no measurement of the 3 sigma is stated.

name: SEQUENTIAL_PATH_DEPENDENT.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to hold the parameter fixed, restrain it, or report the spread between the two directions as its uncertainty.
without: A path-dependent parameter would carry no next step.
opt_in: direction='forward' (default)
note: Three alternatives offered, none picked.

name: SEQUENTIAL_PERSISTENT_FINDING
where: src/rietx/sequential.py:2443-2509 (raise 2503; half-cut src/rietx/sequential.py:2498; MIN_POINTS_FOR_PERSISTENCE src/rietx/sequential.py:2467; exclusions src/rietx/sequential.py:2482)
decides: States, per (code, path), a per-pattern finding that fired on more than half of at least five patterns, at the worst level any occurrence carried, with count/n as its value.
without: The caller would see the finding once per entry (425 BOUND_HIT in the WP-1110 trigger) and never the sentence '42 of 68'.
provenance: WP-1110 item 8, the 68-pattern in-situ series (src/rietx/sequential.py:2446-2454; tests/test_absent_phase.py:376-380)
families: synthetic SeriesResult with the 68-pattern episode's counts (tests/test_absent_phase.py:376)
note: Tier 1 as a statistic per the WP; the open question is whether it carries a verdict. Every raise passes level=levels[(code, path)] (2503), never a literal, so the response test (literal level= at each raise site) cannot read it. The 'more than half' cut is an inline literal the walk cannot see (row-less entry below). Under no deliverable its row prints one line that does not say which per-pattern code persisted (WP Context; tutorial 05, cells 19 and 34).

name: SEQUENTIAL_PERSISTENT_FINDING.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to change the model or the plan.
without: A persistent finding would carry no next step.
note: An instruction to act on every aggregated code alike, including an info one such as DISPERSION_NEGLECTED that the code calls a declared choice (2470-2475).

name: SEQUENTIAL_WIDTH_GROWTH
decides: Names, once per trajectory at its onset, a phase width that reached WIDTH_GROWTH_FACTOR x the first well-measured width, grown by more than WIDTH_GROWTH_SIGMA combined esds, while GoF reached WIDTH_GROWTH_GOF_FACTOR x its own at that reference.
without: A width soaking up a missing component would show only as a rising width and a rising GoF that the caller has to put together.
families: IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real, silent (src/rietx/sequential.py:274-278)
issue #451's operando chain (the reporter's; not on disk)
note: Its three thresholds sit under THRESHOLDS_VERSION, owned by WP-2004: hand the rulings over, bump nothing here. It reads entries above the Rwp fence (2543-2548) that the discontinuity scan drops.

name: SEQUENTIAL_WIDTH_GROWTH.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to fit the onset pattern with the missing component before reading this width, or the phase's scale and cell, as physics.
without: A soaked width would carry no next step.
note: Assumes the cause is a missing component, one of the two readings the docstring names (2516-2519).

name: SEQUENTIAL_MOMENT_HOLD
decides: Counts the patterns on which a site's moment came back unsupported (|m| at or below MOMENT_SUPPORT_SIGMA x its esd), names those with no verdict, and lists up to four successors whose modulus was reseeded to MOMENT_FLOOR_MU_B.
without: The caller would see each entry's magnetic row and no chain-level count, and nothing at all about the floored warm starts.
record: SeriesEntry.magnetic (per-pattern verdicts); the floor carry itself has none
families: real Cr2WO6 4 K/150 K pair, slow (tests/data/gsas2_hb2a_cr2wo6_*; tests/test_magnetic_series.py:1-8)
note: The only report of _floor_unsupported_moments, and it truncates the successor list at four labels (src/rietx/sequential.py:2666-2673). MOMENT_SUPPORT_SIGMA is 2004's (unaudited); MOMENT_FLOOR_MU_B is a tier-3 row.

name: SEQUENTIAL_MOMENT_HOLD.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to plot the trajectory from magnetic_trajectory() and quote these points as held.
without: Held points would carry no next step.

name: SEQUENTIAL_MOMENT_ONSET
decides: Brackets where the moment stops being supported between the last released and first held pattern, read off the verdicts; warns when the bracket's supported side did not converge or verdicts interleave; under direction='both' folds in the reverse chain's bracket and warns on disagreement.
without: The onset would be readable only from magnetic_trajectory(site).onset, with no agreement check between chain directions anywhere in the diagnostics.
families: synthetic magnetic ramp (tests/test_magnetic_series.py:678, tests/test_magnetic_series.py:716, tests/test_magnetic_series.py:956, tests/test_magnetic_series.py:1018, tests/test_magnetic_series.py:1145)
note: Level info or warning at one site (2699, on bracket_verdicts_final), and raised to warning through model_copy in _with_onset_agreement (2784, 2793, 2801, 2810, 2858), which the literal-level response test cannot see: two consequences in one code.

name: SEQUENTIAL_MOMENT_ONSET.suggestion
where: src/rietx/sequential.py:2702; src/rietx/sequential.py:2707; src/rietx/sequential.py:2900; src/rietx/sequential.py:2913; src/rietx/sequential.py:2927; src/rietx/sequential.py:2936
decides: Tells the reader to raise the moment stage's max_iter, to run direction='both', to open the patterns either side of a switch, or to compare the two chains' magnetic rows.
without: An onset would carry no next step.
note: advise() (src/rietx/sequential.py:2779-2781) replaces _RUN_BOTH through model_copy(update=...), a seventh rewrite path the suggestion walk does not count.

name: SIZE_NORMALISED_ACROSS_WAVELENGTHS
decides: States (info) that a shared size column is the coefficient at histogram 0's wavelength and that each histogram's copy carries (lambda_h/lambda_0)^p of it, with the factors and values.
without: A reader would take phases.i.lor_size for the number their own histogram shows.
opt_in: refine_multi / MultiHistogramRefinement.fit: a verb no default path calls (grep of src/rietx 2026-10-24: no caller outside multi.py; refine.py only names it in docstrings at 7701 and 7886)
provenance: WP-1131, WP-1343 (root CLAUDE.md: unfixed, 363.3 A against 623.9 A for one specimen)
families: synthetic two-wavelength LaB6 pair (tests/test_multi_histogram.py:482, tests/test_multi_histogram.py:531, tests/test_multi_histogram.py:634)
note: Reports the size normalisation (row-less entry rietx.params.multi.size_value_scales), which the package applies inside the opt-in verb without being asked; silent when no scaled term moved off zero.

name: SIZE_NORMALISED_ACROSS_WAVELENGTHS.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to read the size with apparent_size_from_size_coefficient at each histogram's own wavelength, or to declare a per-histogram size with SharingMap.
without: The reader would not know how to convert the shared column or opt out of sharing it.
opt_in: refine_multi / MultiHistogramRefinement.fit: a verb no default path calls (grep of src/rietx 2026-10-24: no caller outside multi.py; refine.py only names it in docstrings at 7701 and 7886)

name: PARAMETRIC_OUT_OF_RANGE
decides: Names every subset pattern where a parametric equation's coefficients put the dependent outside its own declared bounds, at the value it took.
without: The dependent's escape would show only by reading each histogram's row against its bounds, since the solve never saw the target's box.
opt_in: parametric=None (default) on MultiHistogramRefinement/refine_multi; the joint verb itself no default path calls
provenance: WP-1325; the WP-1119 hazard one rank up
note: Reports a fact about the caller's own declaration and bounds; no package threshold.

name: PARAMETRIC_OUT_OF_RANGE.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to narrow the subset, lower the polynomial's order, or declare a basis that stays in range.
without: An out-of-range equation would carry no next step.
opt_in: parametric=None (default)

name: PARAMETRIC_TARGET_UNSEEN
decides: Names the subset patterns that cannot see a parametric target's phase, where the target's value and esd are the equation's alone and the form test leaves the pattern out.
without: Those patterns' target values would read as measurements.
opt_in: parametric=None (default)
provenance: WP-1325 (docs/wp/1325-parametric-series.md § Measured: the interval covered a bent truth in the gaps 0.03 of the time)
families: synthetic LaB6 parametric ramp with a faded phase (tests/test_parametric_series.py:617, tests/test_parametric_series.py:541)
note: Rests on the reported support sigma (PHASE_SUPPORT_SIGMA, a tier-3 row) through refine._reported_support_sigma, a package number inside the opt-in switch.

name: PARAMETRIC_TARGET_UNSEEN.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to quote the equation's coefficients, or narrow the subset to the patterns that see the phase.
without: An unseen target would carry no next step.
opt_in: parametric=None (default)

name: PARAMETRIC_FORM_REJECTED
decides: Warns that a parametric equation's form is refused by its data (freeing each pattern's target removes more chi2 than the FORM_TEST_LEVEL point), or that the joint reading rejects all tested equations together without naming one.
without: The coefficients' esds, which assume the form, would be quoted with no test of it.
opt_in: parametric=None (default)
provenance: WP-1325; FORM_TEST_LEVEL 0.95 is a tier-2 row (Venzon & Moolgavkar 1988)
families: Durham ZrP2O7 and WO3, out of sample (src/rietx/schemas/parametric.py:349-352; docs/wp/1325-parametric-series.md § Measured)
note: FORM_TEST_LEVEL and the at-bound hold inside the test (row-less entry rietx.multi._parametric_form_tests:at_bound_hold) are package choices inside the opt-in switch; clash candidate B16 from 2002-batch/clashes.md.

name: PARAMETRIC_FORM_REJECTED.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to add the next term or narrow the subset, one equation at a time when the joint reading alone rejects.
without: A rejected form would carry no next step.
opt_in: parametric=None (default)

name: STAGE_FREED_NOTHING
decides: States (info), per histogram, the stages whose globs reached rows of another histogram and none of this one.
without: A plan whose globs missed a bank would read 'converged' with that histogram's rows never freed (issue #265: Rwp 0.115 against 0.066 with the banks' own globs).
opt_in: refine_multi / MultiHistogramRefinement.fit: a verb no default path calls (grep of src/rietx 2026-10-24: no caller outside multi.py; refine.py only names it in docstrings at 7701 and 7886)
families: TOF bank beside a CW histogram (tests/test_tof_axis.py:1345)
note: Raised only in multi.py. Reports what the stage did, no threshold.

name: STAGE_FREED_NOTHING.suggestion
decides: Tells the reader to list the histogram's parameters and add a glob that reaches them, or scope the stage with hist.<k>.
without: A missed histogram would carry no next step.
opt_in: refine_multi / MultiHistogramRefinement.fit: a verb no default path calls (grep of src/rietx 2026-10-24: no caller outside multi.py; refine.py only names it in docstrings at 7701 and 7886)

name: rietx.schemas.sequential.SeriesEntry.rung
decides: Records which attempt produced the entry's values: the collapsed warm refit, the staged plan from the warm state, or the staged plan cold.
without: The caller could not tell whether a value came from a warm start or a cold restart.
families: synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp (tests/test_sequential.py:915, tests/test_sequential.py:943, tests/test_sequential.py:2082)
note: The first pattern of every chain is 'cold' without a restart, which is why reseeded is a separate field. Default 'warm' only on a document older than WP-1051.

name: rietx.schemas.sequential.SeriesEntry.reseeded
decides: Records that the kept attempt is the cold rung on a warm-startable pattern, so the chain is broken there.
without: The caller could not tell a continuous trajectory point from one with no neighbour behind it.
provenance: WP-0505; WP-1051 (a warm_staged rescue does not set it)
note: Set only when the ladder ran (len(tried) > 1, 1670).

name: rietx.schemas.sequential.SeriesEntry.rwp_fence
decides: Records the Rwp limit the fence set at this pattern: reseed_factor x the median Rwp of the patterns accepted before it.
without: The verdict above_fence and SEQUENTIAL_RWP_OUTLIER could not be re-derived from a reloaded SeriesResult.
note: Written whatever reseed says; None on the first pattern walked or after only quarantined ones.

name: rietx.schemas.sequential.SeriesEntry.rungs_tried
decides: Records every rung attempted on the pattern, in ladder order.
without: rung alone could not say whether the winning attempt was the only one, nor what the iteration count was charged for.
families: IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real, prefix assertion (tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:270)
note: Under reseed=False it is ['warm'] except when a bounded first rung forced an escalation (src/rietx/sequential.py:1561-1571).

name: rietx.schemas.sequential.SeriesEntry.rungs_raised
decides: Records the rungs whose fit raised rather than returned, each with repr(exc), on a pattern a later rung rescued.
without: A raised rung would be indistinguishable from one that returned a worse fit.
provenance: WP-1333, issue #224 (a neighbour's runaway cell refused at compile by every warm rung)
families: synthetic LaB6 with an injected raise (tests/test_series_error_policy.py:302, tests/test_series_error_policy.py:329)

name: rietx.sequential.RESEED_FACTOR
decides: Sets the fence at 1.25 x the median Rwp of the accepted patterns; a warm fit above it climbs the ladder, and a kept fit above it is an outlier.
without: Only divergence would escalate the ladder, so a warm fit converged into a wrong minimum would be kept and seed its successor.
provenance: none stated for 1.25: the comment (src/rietx/sequential.py:167-170) argues for a median over the previous value, not for the factor; WP-1469 carved the outlier case out of it
families: synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp (tests force reseed_factor=1.0: tests/test_sequential.py:663, :802, :929, :954, :977, :1176)
IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real, exercised at its default (tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:258)
note: The WP's open measurement: fence on, off and status-only (diverged or non-finite) on three chain families. Also the default of fit:reseed_factor. Its fence feeds three consumers: the ladder, SEQUENTIAL_RWP_OUTLIER and the discontinuity scan's rejected set.

name: rietx.sequential.FIRST_RUNG_SAMPLES
decides: Requires three converged first rungs before the first-rung budget exists.
without: The budget would arm on one or two samples, whose maximum is set by the cheapest pattern.
invariant: inherits FIRST_RUNG_FACTOR's claim (src/rietx/sequential.py:196-216); no test of its own
provenance: WP-1127: at one sample the bound was 2 x 8 = 16 evaluations on the thermal-ramp chain and its third pattern wanted 17, failing on Linux (src/rietx/sequential.py:176-179)
note: Part of the answer-invariant class with FIRST_RUNG_FACTOR: the bound only exists once it is satisfied.

name: rietx.sequential.FIRST_RUNG_FACTOR
decides: Caps the collapsed first rung at 3.0 x the dearest converged first rung of the chain, after which a truncated rung escalates.
without: A losing first rung would spend the plan's largest budget (~400 evaluations on both harness chains) before the ladder moved on.
invariant: claimed bit-identical, 0 of 1030 and 0 of 392 accepted values (src/rietx/sequential.py:196-216; fit docstring src/rietx/sequential.py:1084-1107); measured by examples/bench_ladder_bound.py, asserted by no test
provenance: WP-1127: legitimate first rung / running max reaches 1.29 over three chains once three samples are in, so 3.0 is 2.3x margin (src/rietx/sequential.py:193-198)
families: synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp (tests/test_sequential.py:1035, tests/test_sequential.py:1099, tests/test_sequential.py:1120)
note: Where it binds it is worth 1.36x the chain's evaluations (src/rietx/sequential.py:1099-1100). WP task 4 writes the invariance test (values bit-identical bound on/off on two chain families, plus the margin). tests/test_sequential.py:1035 shows on a dictated chain that where the bound bites the kept rung and status do change (max_iter kept unbounded, escalated to converged bounded), so the invariance is a measured margin, not a construction. The comment block repeats one paragraph twice (199-216).

name: rietx.sequential.DISCONTINUITY_FACTOR
decides: Calls a step a discontinuity when it exceeds 5.0 x the median absolute step of the same path.
without: The significance leg alone would flag every step of a real ramp with small esds.
provenance: none stated for 5.0: the comment (src/rietx/sequential.py:219-225) justifies needing both legs
note: Keyed to the code the WP removes: goes with it, or is re-tiered as SeriesResult.steps' own (the step size needs no threshold).

name: rietx.sequential.DISCONTINUITY_SIGMA
decides: Requires a flagged step to exceed 3.0 combined esds of its two points.
without: The ratio leg alone would flag noise in a flat series whose median step is near zero.
families: planted perovskite cooling ramp, synthetic null (tests/test_planted_series.py:208)
note: As DISCONTINUITY_FACTOR. A missing esd counts as infinite here (2410-2415, WP-1929).

name: rietx.sequential.MIN_POINTS_FOR_DISCONTINUITY
decides: Scans for discontinuities only on series, and paths, with at least five judged points.
without: A median step over two or three points would set the scale the ratio is taken against.
note: Goes or is re-tiered with the discontinuity code. Also the reason cited for FIRST_RUNG_SAMPLES and MIN_POINTS_FOR_PERSISTENCE.

name: rietx.sequential.MIN_POINTS_FOR_PERSISTENCE
decides: Emits SEQUENTIAL_PERSISTENT_FINDING only on series of at least five patterns.
without: A series of two or three fits would get a 'summary' that repeats its per-entry findings.
provenance: by analogy with MIN_POINTS_FOR_DISCONTINUITY (src/rietx/sequential.py:249-253), no measurement

name: rietx.sequential.NOISE_FLOOR_REL
decides: Ignores a step or a between-chain gap smaller than 1e-9 of the parameter's own magnitude (never below 1e-9 absolute).
without: An unconstrained parameter's floating-point noise would read as a 29 000x jump and as 1e16 sigma of path dependence.
provenance: measured on the synthetic ramp before WP-1938: an unrefinable profile.y with median step 4e-16, one step 1.3e-11, sigma ~4e-55 (src/rietx/sequential.py:229-239)
note: Its absolute floor is the inline max(1.0, magnitude) at src/rietx/sequential.py:2288. A numerical floor (tier-1 candidate); used by both fences.

name: rietx.sequential.PATH_DEPENDENCE_SIGMA
decides: Calls the forward and backward chains in disagreement at more than 3.0 combined esds.
without: SEQUENTIAL_PATH_DEPENDENT would have no cut; every nonzero gap would be a finding or none would.
note: A number defaulted inside the opt-in direction='both' switch, so it is tiered on its own (the record's caller class, condition 2). The GUI serves it as path_dependence_sigma.

name: rietx.sequential.WIDTH_GROWTH_FACTOR
decides: Calls a phase width a soak at 3.0 x the first well-measured width.
without: The GoF leg alone would name every misfit that coincides with any width change.
provenance: WP-1465, issue #451: 3 is the reporter's; operando chain 3.4x at onset, synthetic 3.65x on its second soaked pattern; growth alone fires on 11 of 24 round-robin trajectories against the first value, none against the first measured one (src/rietx/sequential.py:268-278)
note: Under THRESHOLDS_VERSION: ruling handed to WP-2004.

name: rietx.sequential.WIDTH_GROWTH_GOF_FACTOR
decides: Requires GoF at the flagged pattern to reach 2.0 x GoF at the reference.
without: A width that grows for real under a right model would be named a soak.
provenance: WP-1465: clean bound 1.52 over the 75 multi-pattern series the suite runs (thermal ramp's bounded-first-rung fixtures), 1.14 on the round-robin chain; the synthetic soak reads 3.05 (src/rietx/sequential.py:287-296)
families: synthetic real strain growth, GoF flat within 2 % (tests/test_sequential.py:2931)
note: GoF rather than the issue's Rwp (Rwp tracks Rexp). Under THRESHOLDS_VERSION: WP-2004.

name: rietx.sequential.WIDTH_GROWTH_SIGMA
decides: Requires the reference width to be 3.0 of its own esds and the growth 3.0 combined esds.
without: A poorly determined first width (round-robin lor_strain 5.85e-5 with esd 3e3) would make any later value '946x'.
note: Under THRESHOLDS_VERSION: WP-2004.

name: rietx.sequential.refine_sequential:carry
decides: Carries every parameter across the pattern boundary (glob '*').
without: Each pattern would start from the initial models (2863 iterations unchained on round-robin sample 1, against 838 carried).
provenance: WP-0505: 838 iterations carrying everything against 904 excluding scales, Rwp 0.1278 both (src/rietx/sequential.py:668-677); acceptance header (tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:9-20)
note: WP-2002's width twin hold made the policy matter: carry='*' Rwp 0.1256 against restricted 0.1282 and independent 0.1258, a strict xfail at tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:224-229. The GUI passes its own carry (src/rietx/gui/session.py:1699).

name: rietx.sequential.refine_sequential:carry_hkl_intensities
decides: Seeds each warm Le Bail or Pawley pattern's per-hkl intensities from the last accepted pattern, matched by hkl.
without: Every pattern's extraction would restart from scratch.
families: synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp Pawley chain (tests/test_sequential.py:2673)
synthetic LaB6 7-pattern thermal ramp Le Bail chain (tests/test_sequential.py:2245)
note: No effect in Rietveld mode.

name: rietx.sequential.refine_sequential:backend
decides: Runs every pattern on the numpy backend.
without: The caller would have to pick a backend.
provenance: precedent: rietx.refine.refine:backend is tier caller (opt-in extras)
note: Same value and reasoning as the single-fit seat.

name: rietx.sequential.refine_sequential:solver
decides: Runs every pattern on the bounded LM driver (DEFAULT_SOLVER).
without: The caller would have to pick a solver.
provenance: precedent: rietx.refine.refine:solver is tier 2 (GSAS-II's Marquardt-damped solve)
note: Same value as the single-fit seat.

name: rietx.sequential.refine_sequential:history
decides: Keeps no history tree per pattern.
without: A long series would make one tree per pattern and rung.
invariant: precedent: rietx.refine.refine:history is invariant via tests/test_answer_invariant_defaults.py, which does not cover the series seat
note: With history off, entries carry no node_id/tree_id and _link_history writes no warm-start note (src/rietx/sequential.py:1937-1955), so a series' warm-start sources are recorded nowhere (README § Quarantine's record). The GUI passes history=True (src/rietx/gui/session.py:1703).

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:x
decides: Uses the pattern index as the series axis.
without: The caller would have to supply a coordinate.
invariant: presentation: no fitted value reads x (src/rietx/sequential.py:1241-1243); no test asserts it

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:x_label
decides: Names the axis 'index', promoted to 'x' when an x is given.
without: The axis would have no name.
invariant: presentation only; no test asserts it

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:labels
decides: Names each pattern after its source file's stem, else p000.., made unique by position.
without: Patterns would have no names, which become history file names and the key both chains are paired by.
invariant: presentation and pairing only; no fitted value reads it (src/rietx/sequential.py:452-467)
note: Labels are the key path dependence pairs the two chains on (src/rietx/sequential.py:2988-2999).

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:mode
decides: Refines every pattern in Rietveld mode.
without: The caller would have to name a mode.
provenance: precedent: rietx.refine.Refinement.fit:mode is tier 2 (GSAS-II LeBail False)

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:plan
decides: Runs the mccusker_default plan on the first pattern, on every cold rung, and collapsed on every warm one.
without: The caller would have to name a plan.
provenance: precedent: rietx.refine.Refinement.fit:plan is tier 3 (McCusker 1999, the order only)
note: In a series the plan also sets the collapsed first rung's max_iter (the plan's maximum).

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:refit
decides: Makes the collapsed one-stage warm refit the ladder's first rung, rather than the staged plan from the warm state.
without: Every warm pattern would re-walk the staged plan.
provenance: WP-0505: 904 iterations against 1623 staged and 2863 unchained, QPA identical to three decimals (src/rietx/sequential.py:1056-1059)
families: IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real (WP-0505 acceptance)
note: The trigger-series is the counterexample: which rung is cheaper is a property of the model (WP-1127). The GUI keeps a second copy of this default (src/rietx/gui/series.py:75-80).

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:two_theta_limits
decides: Fits every pattern's whole range.
without: The caller would have to state a range.

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:direction
decides: Walks the chain forward only, with no backward chain and no path-dependence comparison.
without: The caller would pay a second complete chain (33.7 s against 83.7 s on the round robin, src/rietx/schemas/sequential.py:776-777) on every series.
opt_in: direction='forward' is the switch's own off default; 'both' is asked by name, and the GUI series panel defaults to 'forward' (src/rietx/gui/series.py:80)
note: Once 'both' is on, PATH_DEPENDENCE_SIGMA and NOISE_FLOOR_REL decide the verdict and the onset agreement raises SEQUENTIAL_MOMENT_ONSET's level, so condition 2 fails for what the switch turns on; the default itself decides nothing. A row at tier caller per the WP is the off default only.

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:reseed
decides: Escalates the ladder when a warm fit diverges or lands above the Rwp fence, keeping the best attempt.
without: Each pattern would keep its first rung; the quarantine still holds (fit docstring src/rietx/sequential.py:1077-1083).
note: With reseed=False a bounded first rung that came back max_iter still escalates (forced, src/rietx/sequential.py:1561-1571).

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:reseed_factor
decides: Sets the fence factor to RESEED_FACTOR (1.25).
without: The caller would have to state a factor.
note: Same value as the constant; one audit covers both.

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:first_rung_factor
decides: Bounds the collapsed first rung at FIRST_RUNG_FACTOR (3.0) x the dearest converged one; None is no bound.
without: Every first rung would run to the plan's own cap.
note: None reproduces every pre-WP-1127 fit bit for bit, the way back a golden declares.

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:verify_discontinuities
decides: Leaves every flagged step unverified by default.
without: Every series flagging s steps would pay up to 2s cold fits (~5 % on the 68-pattern ramp).
opt_in: verify_discontinuities=False (default); the GUI series route does not pass it (src/rietx/gui/session.py:1706-1716)
note: Its input is the discontinuity code's flagged pairs, which the WP replaces.

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:prepare
decides: Calls no per-pattern hook on the warmed models.
without: Nothing: the hook is the caller's code.
opt_in: prepare=None (default); a caller's callable
families: IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real chained arm's seed_scales (tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:105-113, 136)

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:constrain
decides: Declares no per-pattern tie, variable or hold.
without: Nothing: the hook is the caller's code.
opt_in: constrain=None (default); a caller's callable
note: Without it, a tie, variable or hold reaches pattern 1 only (WP-1441).

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:on_result
decides: Calls no per-pattern result callback.
without: Nothing: the callback is the caller's code.
opt_in: on_result=None (default)

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:on_error
decides: Records a pattern on which every rung raised as a SeriesFailure and warm-starts its successor from the last accepted pattern.
without: One pattern's exception would end the chain ('raise', the pre-WP-1333 default).
families: synthetic LaB6 with an injected raise (tests/test_series_error_policy.py:201, tests/test_series_error_policy.py:210)
note: The action it selects is the row-less entry rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement._chain.on_error_carry.

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:events
decides: Attaches no event callback.
without: Nothing: an observation channel.
invariant: precedent: rietx.refine.Refinement.fit:events is invariant via tests/test_answer_invariant_defaults.py, which does not cover the series seat

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:cancel
decides: Passes no cancel token (a recorded run still composes one for rietx watch).
without: Nothing: an observation channel.
invariant: precedent: rietx.refine.Refinement.fit:cancel is invariant; no series test

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:progress
decides: Writes no progress lines.
without: Nothing: an observation channel.
invariant: precedent: rietx.refine.Refinement.fit:progress is invariant; no series test

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:telemetry
decides: Records the series as one run directory.
without: Nothing about the answer: the recorder sits beside the stream.
invariant: precedent: rietx.refine.Refinement.fit:telemetry is invariant; no series test

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement.fit:label
decides: Leaves the series' run directory unnamed, so rietx watch shows the pattern labels alone.
without: Nothing about the answer: a run's name.
invariant: precedent: rietx.refine.Refinement.fit:label is invariant; no series test

name: rietx.sequential._prefer
decides: Chooses which attempt of a pattern's ladder is kept: an untruncated attempt over a truncated one, then a non-diverged over a diverged one, then the lower Rwp (_better).
without: The last rung tried would be kept whatever it reached.
provenance: WP-1051 (_better); WP-1127 (_prefer: measured that _better alone keeps a truncated rung at equal Rwp, src/rietx/sequential.py:1977-1980)
families: IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real (tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:276-278: kept Rwp <= rwp_warm)
note: Keeping the best attempt is one of Rule 1's protections; the criterion (Rwp, with 'max_iter' ranked equal to 'converged' in _better at 1960-1962) is what is on trial. No field records a middle rung's Rwp (rwp_of is local, 1543).

name: rietx.sequential._reseed_needed
decides: Rejects an attempt that diverged or whose Rwp is above the fence; 'max_iter' is not tested.
without: No rung after the first would ever run.
provenance: WP-0505; the narrowness argued in the module docstring (src/rietx/sequential.py:87-104): guard findings and discontinuities were rejected as triggers
note: The second review's status-only alternative (diverged or non-finite) changes this function; the WP's three-family measurement compares on, off and status-only.

name: rietx.sequential._ladder
where: src/rietx/sequential.py:539-566; RUNGS src/rietx/sequential.py:356-360; stop test src/rietx/sequential.py:1559-1571
decides: Sets the escalation order (collapsed warm, staged from warm, staged cold under refit='single'; staged warm then cold under 'stages'), runs a rung only while the fence rejects the best attempt so far, and gives up after the cold rung.
without: A rejected warm fit would go straight to the cold fit, paying ~3x to discard a warm start not shown to be the problem (pre-WP-1051).
provenance: WP-1051: 838-904 iterations warm-collapsed, 1623 warm-staged, 2863 cold on round-robin sample 1 (src/rietx/sequential.py:550-555)
families: IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real, prefix assertion (tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:258)
note: Rungs, order and give-up point are the choices to tier. A raised rung escalates like a diverged one (WP-1333). The cold rung starts from the initial models, so a quarantined pattern has no fourth option.

name: rietx.sequential._first_rung_budget
where: src/rietx/sequential.py:569-601; _bounded_plan src/rietx/sequential.py:604-620; armed src/rietx/sequential.py:1537-1539; forced escalation src/rietx/sequential.py:1561; sample src/rietx/sequential.py:1720-1722
decides: Caps the collapsed first rung's evaluations at first_rung_factor x the dearest converged first rung once FIRST_RUNG_SAMPLES are in hand, and forces an escalation when the capped rung returns max_iter.
without: A losing first rung would spend the plan's whole budget before the ladder moved on.
record: none: no field says a rung was truncated or what the budget was; only rungs_tried shows the escalation
invariant: claimed at src/rietx/sequential.py:196-216 and src/rietx/sequential.py:1084-1107; bench examples/bench_ladder_bound.py; no test
note: Inert under refit='stages' (1535-1539). The cold fit is deliberately not evidence (src/rietx/sequential.py:585-597: cold 9 evaluations, warm 14 on the suite's cheap plan).

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement._chain.quarantine
decides: A pattern whose kept attempt diverged seeds no successor, joins no median and supplies no first-rung sample; its successor warm-starts from the last accepted pattern.
without: One failed pattern would seed its neighbour with garbage and drag the median that sets every later fence (pre-WP-1051).
record: SeriesEntry.status ('diverged'); SeriesEntry.rung; SeriesEntry.rungs_tried; no field names the successors seeded from an earlier pattern instead
families: IUCr CPD round-robin sample-1 1a-1h, real, never fires (tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:284-285)
note: One of Rule 1's four protections; kept unless a competent caller wants a diverged fit to seed its successors (WP Context). Holds under reseed=False. Missing record: README § Quarantine's record.

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement._chain.rwp_outlier_carve_out
where: src/rietx/sequential.py:1688-1697; scan exclusion src/rietx/sequential.py:2387-2390; verdict src/rietx/schemas/sequential.py:193-209
decides: Keeps a pattern whose best rung is still above the fence in the chain (it seeds its successor and joins the median), while dropping its steps from the discontinuity scan.
without: Quarantined, the median would never follow a lasting change and every later pattern would climb the ladder (+55 % iterations, 18 of 18 flagged against 7, on a 24-pattern ramp whose counts fall 4x).
provenance: WP-1469, issue #481: on #481's blank quarantine buys 2-8 % of the chain, values identical to the digit (src/rietx/sequential.py:1688-1696)
families: planted perovskite cooling ramp, synthetic (tests/test_planted_series.py:130, tests/test_planted_series.py:146)
note: The exception WP-1469 carved out of the reseed fence. The scan exclusion is what let the planted step behind a blank frame be seen (src/rietx/sequential.py:2375-2386).

name: rietx.sequential._floor_unsupported_moments
where: src/rietx/sequential.py:857-922; called src/rietx/sequential.py:1704-1706; carried src/rietx/sequential.py:1529-1530; reported src/rietx/sequential.py:1361, 2654, 2666-2673
decides: Before an accepted pattern's state seeds its successor, scales every modulus its fit called unsupported down to MOMENT_FLOOR_MU_B, keeping its direction and leaving the entry's own value untouched.
without: A stale modulus would seed the next pattern, where |F_m|^2 ~ m^2 gives no gradient to leave it, and the chain would print a smooth |m| through the transition.
record: none: only SEQUENTIAL_MOMENT_HOLD's message, which names at most four successors; the floored dict _chain returns (1745) reaches no field
provenance: WP-1329 (WP-1301's rule along the series); MOMENT_FLOOR_MU_B is a tier-3 row (WP-1327); MOMENT_SUPPORT_SIGMA is 2004's, unaudited
families: synthetic magnetic ramp (tests/test_magnetic_series.py:587, tests/test_magnetic_series.py:609, tests/test_magnetic_series.py:618, tests/test_magnetic_series.py:1065, tests/test_magnetic_series.py:1194)
note: Not in the first plan; the review found it. Acts whatever reseed says; a None verdict is never floored (892-894); on_error='skip' clears the pending floor (1647). A protection that records only in prose.

name: rietx.sequential._carry_into
decides: Copies every fitted value matching the carry globs into the next pattern's initial models, carrying a refined coordinate as its site's displacement and a rigid body's orientation and torsions, then re-derives every tie from its carried sources.
without: Each pattern would start from the initial models.
record: none on the SeriesResult; with history on, the root annotation series_warm_start_tree/_node (src/rietx/sequential.py:1937-1955)
provenance: WP-0505 (src/rietx/sequential.py:668-677); WP-1333 coordinate displacement; WP-1805/1808 rigid bodies
note: The carry policy x the width twin hold is a WP clash item (strict xfail tests/test_acceptance_sequential.py:224-229).

name: rietx.sequential._reanchor_carried
decides: Rebases a carried displacement DOF's anchor against its source when the constrain hook ties it to a named variable, so the variable's warm start is not added twice.
without: A tied coordinate would gain the previous displacement again on every pattern.
note: Arithmetic correctness of the carry (a tier-1 candidate).

name: rietx.sequential._carry_variables
decides: Warms each named variable the constrain hook declared from the last accepted pattern's value under the carry globs, skipping a variable tied to others.
without: A vars.X would restart from its declaration on every pattern though carry=['*'] claims it is carried.

name: rietx.sequential._collapse
decides: Builds the default warm rung: one stage freeing the union of the plan's globs at the plan's largest max_iter and lebail_cycles, no stage seed, the largest strain_seed, and the plan's intermediate_ftol, closing_window_tol, lebail_passes and phase_support_sigma.
without: Every warm pattern would re-walk the staged plan.
record: StageResult.name 'warm_refit' on the per-pattern RefinementResult (SequentialRefinement.results_), not on SeriesEntry
provenance: WP-0505; WP-1123; WP-1323; WP-2002 B1 and sixth round Q1/Q2; the dropped seed measured on the LaB6 ramp, chi2_red 1.05828 seeded against 1.05145 (src/rietx/sequential.py:478-488)
note: Carries the closing stage (closing_window_tol), 1.05-2.05x a single fit's time a pattern; its cost along a chain and its effect on path dependence are unmeasured (WP Context; closing stage x path dependence is a clash item).

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement._verify_discontinuities
decides: Refits each flagged step's two patterns cold and independently and records the signed cold step over the chain's as the discontinuity diagnostic's value.
without: The step would carry no reproduction ratio; the reader would run the cold pair by hand.
record: Diagnostic.value on SEQUENTIAL_DISCONTINUITY (not a SeriesStep field)
opt_in: verify_discontinuities=False (default); no default path passes it
provenance: WP-1305: ~5 % on the 68-pattern thermal ramp, four steps over four patterns (src/rietx/sequential.py:1117-1124)
note: Moves no fitted value, entry, rung or median (fit docstring 1126-1130). Which pairs it refits is the tier-3 discontinuity pick, so its input moves with that ruling. Each cold refit pays the automatic moment-angle profile interval (no _auto_intervals gate in sequential.py, WP task 3).

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement._chain.on_error_carry
decides: When every rung of a pattern raised, records a SeriesFailure and warm-starts the successor from the last accepted pattern ('carry'), cold ('skip'), or ends the chain ('raise'); a series that fitted nothing raises under every policy.
without: One pattern's exception would lose every converged pattern of the chain.
record: SeriesResult.failures; SeriesResult.n_failed; SeriesEntry.rungs_raised on a rescued pattern
note: Its default is the fit:on_error row; 'carry' is quarantine's own treatment of a diverged fit (1648-1652).

name: rietx.sequential._persistent_diagnostics.half
decides: Promotes a per-pattern finding to the series only when it fired on more than half the patterns.
without: Every per-pattern finding, or none, would be restated for the series.
provenance: docstring: 'a change of subject, not a sensitivity' (src/rietx/sequential.py:2456-2462); no measurement
note: An inline literal (count * 2 <= n) the constant walk cannot see.

name: rietx.sequential.NOT_A_SERIES_FINDING
decides: Excludes FROZEN_COMPILE_STALE from SEQUENTIAL_PERSISTENT_FINDING's aggregation.
without: A chain whose last stages move the zero and widths would carry a series warning about compile sizing on every pattern (round-robin sample 1: 1.3-2.1e-2).
note: A frozenset of codes, which the walk cannot see.

name: rietx.sequential._WIDTH_SUFFIXES
decides: Sets which phase widths the soak test reads (lor_strain, lor_size, gauss_strain, gauss_size) and judges the Gaussian pair on their square root.
without: A Stephens block or another width would be screened, or none would.
note: A dict, which the walk cannot see. A series refining a Stephens block is not screened.

name: rietx.sequential._relative_paths
decides: Leaves coordinate and rigid-body rotation DOFs (steps, not positions) out of both fences and compares moment angles modulo a turn.
without: A chained coordinate DOF's first step would read as a jump on every clean series, and its opposite signs in the two chains as path dependence.
note: Arithmetic (tier-1 candidate); the coordinate rows they drive are judged instead.

name: rietx.sequential.SequentialRefinement._fit_one.declared_wavelengths
decides: Threads the series root's declared wavelength into each pattern's WAVELENGTH_CALIBRATION reference, though the carried refined wavelength stays the warm start.
without: Each pattern would report the pattern-to-pattern drift (~0 ppm) instead of the move from what the beamline stated.
note: Moves no fitted value, only a diagnostic's reference; skipped when a prepare hook changes the line count.

name: rietx.multi._hold_unsupported_phases_multi
decides: Holds for the stage every joint column whose every reached entry is structure of a phase below phase_support_sigma wherever it lives (a shared cell only when no histogram sees the phase), and a phase's scale only where no histogram's range has a line of it.
without: An unseen phase's shared cell would walk at unchanged Rwp (14.9 A from truth in the single-fit v1.3 measurement).
opt_in: refine_multi / MultiHistogramRefinement.fit: a verb no default path calls (grep of src/rietx 2026-10-24: no caller outside multi.py; refine.py only names it in docstrings at 7701 and 7886)
note: The joint runner reads CompiledModel.phase_support at stage start and answer alike, never the single fit's scale significance (refine._answer_significance, WP-1523), so the two runners call a phase unseen by different statistics (src/rietx/multi.py:413-417). No Le Bail/Pawley force-fix exists here: the joint fit refuses those modes (src/rietx/multi.py:1180-1184; src/rietx/params/multi.py:234). The 2002 row StageResult.held covers the single runner's hold.

name: rietx.multi._rehold_multi
where: src/rietx/multi.py:707-761; called src/rietx/multi.py:1545-1547; second solve src/rietx/multi.py:1583-1631
decides: At the answer, releases a held phase that is seen again and restores to its stage start and holds a column whose phase collapsed while solving, then solves once more.
without: A phase that appeared mid-stage would stay held, and one that vanished would keep the cell it walked to.
opt_in: refine_multi / MultiHistogramRefinement.fit: a verb no default path calls (grep of src/rietx 2026-10-24: no caller outside multi.py; refine.py only names it in docstrings at 7701 and 7886)
